## Fresh independent integrated assessment

Assessed the complete seven-file engineering diff from9af7fcd9198471d044fec61f2c22f4fbcd781d7b through53bd5746 on fix/npm-publication-visibility, including the original npm waiting correction and four subsequent CI-repair files. This reviewer authored none of it. User-authorized bounded repair and the existing Release ordinary-CI/publication distinction govern; no new Design package or planned milestone is selected. R1 and previous Verify remain historical/stale rather than being reused as current approval.

The original polling change still gives npm121 post-write observations with120 capped-backoff waits while other boundaries retain6. A single publish remains outside the observation loop; matching/conflicting identity exits early and timeout preserves uncertainty/recovery evidence. The README describes an approximate20-minute observation window, not an availability guarantee.

The new candidate correction removes only refs/tags/<current stable tag> inside prepare_candidate's disposable inner clone, and only when ci_only is selected. Derived stable input validation precedes the deletion. Original checkout/tag, unrelated tags and public state are unchanged. Actual release preparation does not take that branch and retains strict local-tag preflight. This restores the adopted requirement that ordinary CI may check already-published source without pretending it is publication-eligible. CI-only candidate publication rejection and hosted public-version eligibility remain unchanged. No preflight protection is universally disabled.

The added test creates an actual local release tag and exercises the real builder/preflight twice: ordinary release rejects the conflict, CI-only reaches the next npm installation boundary, and the original tag/source remain intact. Its deliberate stop before npm-ci is scoped preflight/invariance proof, not full candidate or CI proof. Existing full authoritative replacement PR execution is separately required by Verify; no old passing PR run is claimed to cover changed scripts.

Error reporting adds only numeric errno when present, preserving private message/path redaction. The diagnostic regression covers FileNotFoundError2 plus prior failure shapes through actual dispatch. This improves future diagnosis without claiming the earlier generic hosted OSError was conclusively a tag conflict. No unsupported root-cause claim or success substitution is made.

## First-pass checklist

1. Spec alignment: pass — existing Release ordinary-CI offline/published-source distinction and REL-SR-14/15/23 bounded observation/identity contract.
2. Test coverage: pass — new tag/diagnostic regressions fail before and pass after; original delayed-visibility single-write regression remains passing. Broader34 focused candidate/approval/coordination proof inspected.
3. Edge cases: pass — published local tag differs for CI and real release; original refs remain intact; absent tag deletion is idempotent; npm last-poll match and earlier timeout/conflict behavior remain bounded.
4. Error handling: pass — actual preflight failure still rejects release, CI repair does not create publication permission, numeric diagnostics remain redacted, exhausted publication observation still records failure.
5. Architecture boundaries: pass — same candidate builder/coordinator/provider and existing operation identities; only disposable clone state changes for CI.
6. Compatibility: pass — canonical release checks and hosted publication eligibility remain strict; no source/public tag mutation, entrypoint change or new record format.
7. Security/privacy: pass — no extra credentials/authorization, no public write or private-path exposure introduced.
8. Derived artifact currency: pass within review scope — no manually generated package metadata; corrected CI still uses actual builder/full checks. Full replacement PR proof remains pending, not inferred from focused tests.
9. Unrelated changes: pass — initial minimal fix plus scoped CI-only repair and diagnostic clarity only.
10. Validation evidence: pass for implementation judgment — exact regression red/green evidence and focused suite assessed with fresh independent targeted execution. Required PR/Verify readiness is expressly not claimed before its actual completion.

## Actual checks and handoff

Independently ran PYTHONPATH=scripts python -m unittest release_candidate_tests.ReleaseCandidateIntegrationTests.test_ci_candidate_preserves_published_tag_without_release_eligibility release_coordination_tests.ReleaseCoordinationTests.test_actual_ci_dispatch_does_not_report_private_diagnostics release_execution_tests.ReleaseExecutorTests.test_delayed_npm_visibility_completes_without_duplicate_publication:3 tests passed in6.858s. git diff --check passed. Inspected recorded ci-repair-proof, the prior40-test polling evidence, new34-test focused success, failing-before tag/diagnostic logs and recorded test hashes.

The full authoritative PR command is running on53bd5746 with the real publishedv1.0.0 tag fetched to reproduce that boundary. This review makes no claim about its result, hosted CI, actual npm publication or fresh Verify. Verify must inspect that replacement result and all current evidence before readiness; a new failure returns to its owner. Read-only source/provider/workflow context establishes scope, not remote setup. No implementation, route, work, finding disposition or external state was changed by this assessment.
independence_basis: Independent nonauthor reviewed the complete initial fix plus CI-repair diff afresh and independently reran three direct regressions; authored no implementation/test/guidance. R1 is not reused as final approval.
